first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that shorter onboarding and simpler signup improved completion, time-to-value, and first-week activation. This addresses both observed declines without the margin and customer-quality risks of reacting to competitor pricing. Verification should confirm experiment design, segment coverage, and whether gains extended beyond early-stage metrics; sustainable qualified-revenue impact remains uncertain until tested.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding, with emphasis on self-serve SMB accounts. The closest prior test improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly matching the current completion and activation declines. Signup simplification also produced 4% qualified-revenue growth in SMBs, but its 1% retention decline warrants retention and qualified-revenue guardrails. Promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but has less verified evidence here on downstream customer quality and margin sustainability.
